newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INSIGHT - NZ dlr opens well-bid, breaks US$0.6880.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NZ dlr opens well-bid, breaks US$0.6880.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar broke through resistance at US$0.6880 on Monday and was expected to push higher if weakness in the Trade-Weighted Index persisted.
By 9.25 a.m. (2125 GMT) the currency was at US$0.6900/07, up from 0.6878/85 at Friday's close, having traded a 0.6868-95 range over the weekend.
The Trade-Weighted Index was at 67.66, up from 67.53 at the open, but weaker than Friday's 67.87 finish.
"The Kiwi has been well-supported this morning and in late New York and that's the result of the lower TWI," said one dealer.
The lower TWI was a reflection of weakness on some cross rates, particulary the mark and the yen, which had encouraged exporter buying.

"That's where we've seen all the buying coming through and we imagine that, whilst a decent tranche of that (buying) has been done now, as dollar/yen moves lower through this 120 area we feel Kiwi will stay well-supported," he said.
He expected US$0.6880 to form a base for the Kiwi.
Technical analysis suggested the break over 0.6890 meant continued strength up to 0.6920/40, possibly higher, said Keith Black at the Bank of New Zealand.
He wrote in a commentary that only a drop below 0.6880/90, then 0.6850/60 would revive a bearish outlook for the currency.
